newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Sept 18.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Sept 18.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning.
** Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) seen opening weak after two successive holidays, traders say
** State Bank of India's GDR issue goes before federal cabinet committee tomorrow for approval, says The Economic Times. The report says the finance minister has cleared the $400 million issue

** Financial Express reports that cabinet will also decide tomorrow whether foreign institutional investors should be allowed to increase their stake in SBI to 24 percent from the current 20 percent ceiling
** Former telecommunications minister Sukh Ram, arrested by authorities on arrival from London on Monday night, detained till September 23 by a New Delhi court in connection with a telecom scandal
** Cancellation of diesel imports by India's leading refiner on Tuesday, due to port delays, highlights the infrastructural constraints holding back the country's ambitious growth plans, analysts say
The state-run Indian Oil Corporation cancelled a tender to import high speed diesel citing port congestion. Earlier this year, it had cancelled two tenders for kerosene imports, traders said

** Indian firms planning to access overseas equity markets through the global depositary receipt (GDR) route will find the going tough in the near term. Institutional investors say only top quality GDR issues will be accepted, the Business Line newspaper reports
** The 50-stocks National Stock Exchange (NSE) index .NSEI rose nine points to close at 961 on Tuesday as punters covered short positions in end-account trade
** The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) was shut on Monday and Tuesday for Hindu festivals. Last Friday, the 30-share BSE index closed 44.17 points or 1.3 percent lower at 3347.37
** The 100-share National index fell 14.45 points or 0.95 percent to 1512.42 on Friday

** Last week, Bombay's benchmark 30-share index slumped 160.70 points or 4.8 percent to 3347.37 after the government failed to deliver anticipated tax reliefs, including a waiver of a minimum corporate tax proposed in the government's July budget
